title: What can you say about 5-HTP in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for 5-HTP; the strongest is "Helps promote a healthy mood balance" (moderate, 150-300 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats depression or anxiety".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps promote a healthy mood balance.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 150-300 mg a day; no other listed source covers 5-HTP.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; take with food. Health Canada: start low and build up over 2 weeks to limit stomach upset, and use it for at least 2 weeks to see an effect.

supported_wordings.wording: With a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity, helps with weight management by reducing carbohydrate cravings.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 750-900 mg a day with diet and exercise; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; at most 300 mg per dose, taken 30 minutes before meals. Health Canada asks for a practitioner's advice beyond 12 weeks for products giving over 600 mg a day, and says not to use it in pregnancy.

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names mental health disorders. Health Canada asks people with a psychological disorder such as anxiety or depression to consult a practitioner before use.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: A natural antidepressant, or works like Prozac or an SSRI
wordings_to_avoid.why: Compares the product to a drug class. FDA's 2000 rule (page 1027) cites 'Herbal Prozac' as wording that ties a product to an approved drug.
Names a sleep disorder. FDA's 2000 rule (page 1031) reads sleep wording as disease wording unless it is limited to occasional sleeplessness.
Names diseases. Health Canada lists both uses, but they are condition uses (see notes).
FDA's 2000 rule (page 1026) counts obesity as a disease; the supported wording is weight management with diet and exercise.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1012

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
